content:
Hello,

I am trying to define some custom syntax in a new syntax category. However, when I do so, it seems to conflict with syntax in other categories.

  declare_syntax_cat new_stx_cat

  syntax "stx" : new_stx_cat

I thought this use of declare_syntax_cat would keep this new syntax "separate" from existing syntax. However, if I now try to use "stx" as, for instance, the name of a function, I get an error.

  def stx : Nat -> Nat | x => x -- unexpected token 'stx'; expected identifier

How can I prevent this conflict?

Hi, syntax "stx" adds stx to the table of reserved keywords regardless of syntax category. You can use syntax &"stx" : new_stx_cat to suppress this. See the 'Syntax Specifiers' block here in the Lean Language Reference.
You can also do what tactics do and use declare_syntax_cat new_stx_cat (behavior := symbol).
That only affects the behavior for the first token though, so any others will still have to use &"..."
Wonderful, both of these solutions worked for me. Thank you!
